name: Almendralejo – Purificación church tower & memorial
story: On the drive north from Seville, Asensio's and Castejón's columns entered Almendralejo on 7 August 1936. About fifty militiamen barricaded themselves in the tower of the parish church of Nuestra Señora de la Purificación and held out for a week against artillery, explosives and smoke before surrendering; they were then shot. The town suffered heavy repression, including the killing of a number of women. A memorial in the municipal cemetery, unveiled in November 2023, names 462 victims from Almendralejo and 252 from other towns killed nearby. Earlier, under Republican control, several right-wing prisoners had also been killed in the town.
see: The tall church tower on Plaza de España, still showing its role in the siege only through local accounts; the new memorial wall in the municipal cemetery.
plan: The church exterior is free on Plaza de España; the cemetery lies at the edge of town (usual cemetery hours).

boxes.text: Numbers killed after the capture vary widely: some accounts give 28 on entry, Portuguese journalists reported up to 1,000; the 2023 memorial names 714 victims (town + other localities). The number of right-wing victims killed earlier in the town is also debated.
